title: Typography / Uber Move and display pairings
slide_intent: Give words a consistent voice and differentiate leading from supporting text so readers can hear the hierarchy.
strategic_value: The source ties Uber Move to clarity, consistency and brand equity; its two weight pairings can maintain that voice across partner messages.
demonstration: A black specimen panel compares Display and Text in four weights. A white panel below compares Medium/Light and Bold/Regular headline–subhead pairings.
practical_value: Choose Display for headlines and subheads, Text for body copy, and one of the stated display weight pairs.

content_islands.name: Typeface roles
content_islands.spec: Place the Uber Move explanation in the upper left beside Display and Text columns, each showing Light, Regular, Medium and Bold in white on black.

content_islands.name: Display pairings
content_islands.spec: Place the pairing instructions in the lower left beside two options: Medium header with Light subhead, and Bold header with Regular subhead.

ingredient.name: Uber Move families and weights
ingredient.role: Establish a recognizable typographic voice and separate information levels.
ingredient.application: Use Display for headlines/subheads and Text for body copy; pair Medium with Light or Bold with Regular.
ingredient.scope: October 2018 partner guide; this page’s pairing rule is labeled Display.

reference_purposes.Intent: The source says Uber Move maintains consistency, creates clarity and provides brand equity; pairings support hierarchy.
reference_purposes.Expression: Display and Text specimens show four weights and two contrasting pairs.
reference_purposes.Application: The page assigns Display to headlines/subheads and Text to body copy.
